ratings_why.fun: Placing fodder and gaps around Lids is a real puzzle each turn, and a chain of Springs is a great fight moment, though the late Spring stack is a lot to follow.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: the board your opponent previews is a row of closed Lids, so hidden information enters an auto-battler, and the wait-or-strike pull splits one tribe into two real builds.

verdict_why: The tribe reads well and the fantasy lands, but a few rules (Lids in the front row, Wafer-Lid Sentry's interrupted attack, the Master's trigger) don't yet say what happens.

points.text: Lurk doesn't say whether a front row holding only Lids counts as empty, so a player can't tell if the enemy now hits the back row. Say it outright, since the Patient build lives on this.
Wafer-Lid Sentry doesn't say whether the enemy's own attack still happens after the Spring attack hits it, or what happens if the Spring attack kills it. Add one clause.

The Worshipful Master's rule clashes with Lurk's own 'all your other units are under Lids' Spring, and on a Patient board with Lurkers that never open it may never Spring. Say which rule wins, and show on screen the list of Spring effects it will repeat.
The Lodge regalia (ballot, Tyler, passwords) is mostly in the names; a card whose knock must come from a specific neighbour, like a password, would put the club in the play too.
Show a re-closed Lid in a different colour from a fresh one, so players can see which Lurkers Corkhinge has already reset.

standouts.why: Signora Corkhinge reads at a glance and is the trapdoor itself: strike, then the lid shuts again.
Heath Wolf Mother is short, on theme (hatchlings off her back) and her Spiderlings become the next knocks.
Tapwell grows whichever way you play him, which teaches both builds from Tier 1.

weakest.why: The Worshipful Master asks the player to remember every Spring effect from the fight so far; too much to read in one look.
Grit-Dresser is a plain buffer with no tie rule for 'lowest Attack' and little spider in what it does.
Ballooning Money Spider is a generic death-summon; the ballooning, lucky-spider fantasy doesn't show up in its play.

flags.note: Its Spring condition overrides Lurk's own rule without saying so, and the repeat list is invisible state.
Doesn't say whether the interrupted enemy attack still goes ahead.
Double-damage Cleave Spring attacks on an all-Lurker board give a big free opening at Start of Combat.
Repeating Start of Combat effects on every Spring depends on other tribes' cards, so its ceiling is unknown.
